prize_parts.citation: for developing methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets, which made empirical industrial organisation quantitative

statement.case_for: The Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes framework (random-coefficients discrete choice with endogenous prices, plus Berry's inversion) gave economists a way to recover substitution patterns and market power from market-level data. Together with the Ericson-Pakes dynamic industry framework, it made it possible to ask and answer welfare and counterfactual questions that were previously out of reach. The scientific reach is very wide. The methods are used in merger review, antitrust and regulation, and also in trade, health, environmental and energy economics. The work is about three decades old and has been tested through daily use by academics, agencies and industry. Attribution is also the cleanest of the shortlist candidates I find strongest. The core estimator is the BLP trio's work, and Pakes also carries the dynamic-games and estimation programme. I see this as a discovery about how markets can be measured, not only a technical advance, because it changed which questions about competition and welfare can be answered with data. I rank it first on the common criteria of impact, attribution clarity and maturity, not on how many colleagues listed it.
statement.case_against: Only four members ranked B029, and several colleagues did not rank it at all. This could reflect distance from the field, but it also means the case has been tested by fewer committee readers than the labour and trade candidates. The ballot credits seven names, and a three-person cap leaves out Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, whose contributions are real, so the exclusion is contestable. The prize could also be read as a methods prize rather than a prize for economic discoveries, and a methods prize would sit uneasily so soon after 2021. B022 has the broadest and deepest support, with its China-shock evidence clearly attributable to Autor, Dorn and Hanson. B012 offers a very clean two-person attribution and has had two decades of confirmation, and trade has not been recognised since 2008. If B029's attribution proves less settled than I think, one of those two should take precedence.

responses.point: Fredriksson ranked B029 first, found the BLP trio the cleanest attribution, and flagged the risk of a second methods prize soon after the 2021 causal-inference award.
responses.response: I agree on attribution. The 2021 prize recognised identification from natural experiments, which is a different contribution from structural demand estimation and dynamic oligopoly models. The BLP and Ericson-Pakes methods allow counterfactuals for prices, mergers and welfare, which design-based methods generally cannot provide. I still take the methods-versus-discovery concern seriously. The citation should name market power and competition as the subject, not the estimator.

responses.point: Friberg ranked B029 third with the same trio, and asked whether Bresnahan should displace one of the BLP co-authors because the seven-name list suggests diffuse credit.
responses.response: Bresnahan's earlier work on estimating demand and market power in differentiated-product industries is substantial, and I do not dismiss it. I still keep the BLP trio. The lasting tool is the estimator that handles endogenous prices with market-level data and flexible substitution patterns, and that is Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes. Pakes then adds the dynamic-games contribution. I would revisit this if colleagues who know the empirical IO literature argue that Bresnahan's priority should outweigh Levinsohn's role. I hold this view with moderate confidence.

responses.point: Hassler ranked B021 first and B022 fifth, and proposed only Autor and Hanson for B022 because credit for the task framework and for the China-shock work is blurred and Dorn's role is secondary.
responses.response: The credit split is a real problem for B022. The task framework owes much to people outside the credited set, notably Acemoglu, who was recognised in 2024. I would not drop Dorn from a trade-shock citation, because the China-shock papers are joint work by Autor, Dorn and Hanson. If B022 is chosen, I would tie the citation narrowly to the effects of trade and technology on local labour markets, and I think the trio is more defensible than the pair. I disagree mildly with Hassler on Dorn but agree that the citation scope must be tightened.

responses.point: Boppart ranked B012 first. Melitz is the clear originator, Helpman is central, a two-person award is clean, and trade has not been recognised since 2008.
responses.response: I did not rank B012 in my top eight, and Boppart's case is strong on attribution and maturity. I have no scientific objection to a Melitz-Helpman award. My hesitation is that parts of the empirical foundation, such as exporter premia, and later quantitative work by Bernard, Eaton-Kortum and Redding sit outside the two names. Helpman's other candidacy, B007, also complicates how his body of work would be recognised. I regard B012 as the strongest competitor on clarity of credit, and it is a candidate I should have weighed more in my opening.

responses.point: Teorell ranked B022 first with only Autor and Hanson, because the identification is credible and the questions are of first-order importance, but he noted that task-model credit is diffuse beyond the credited set.
responses.response: I agree that the identification strategy and the importance of the question are real strengths, and they are why I keep B022 as an alternative. I part ways on the two-person framing. Excluding Dorn would make the China-shock part harder to defend on attribution, and relying on the task literature would make it harder still, because that literature extends beyond the credited names. Teorell's own point about diffuse task credit is the main reason I rank B022 below B029 on attribution.

uncertainties: Whether Bresnahan's early demand-estimation work should displace Levinsohn or Berry in the trio, and whether Pakes alone should be recognised for the dynamic-industry work.
Whether the committee reads B029 as a methods prize or as a prize for economic discovery, given the 2021 econometrics prize.
How strongly the narrow support for B029 reflects distance from the field versus a real difference in merit.
Whether the Autor-Dorn-Hanson trade-shock evidence can be separated from the broader task framework, whose credit lies partly outside the credited names.
My recollection of contribution details and priority is from general knowledge and not independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent for B029 from the supplied profile: none of Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn is among my listed co-authors or institutions. I have co-authored with Timo Boppart (co-opted member) and with John Hassler (chair), and both are discussed above. Those relationships do not bear on the candidates. For the alternative B047, the profile does not show a link to Persson, Tabellini or Besley, but Persson is based in Stockholm, so institutional proximity may exist that the profile does not record. This is disclosed, not adjudicated.
